instagram_caption:
A scratched little reel held footage everyone thought was gone. 🎞️

Fritz Lang premiered Metropolis in 1927 at about two and a half hours. Soon it was trimmed, and for decades the cut scenes could not be seen. Even careful restorations were missing about a quarter of the film.

In 2008 a curator at the Museo del Cine in Buenos Aires pulled out old reels until she found a scene nobody knew. The story goes that a collector carried a print to Argentina in 1928. More than twenty minutes came back, badly scratched.

A restored version premiered in Berlin in 2010. The restorers kept the scratched shots rather than dropping them.

The twist: it was never hidden. The museum had been on a distribution list since the 1920s. Someone just had to ask.
